issues.description: The problem statement's UML and the solution expect Stock to provide a method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), but the template Stock implementation defines addItem(StockIngredient) instead. This method-name/signature mismatch is structural: students implementing SealSaloon (or following the UML) will look for addToStockIngredients and may either fail to compile or be confused by the differing API in the provided template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the UML and solution by renaming or adding the method: either rename addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) or add a forwarding addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) method that delegates to addItem. Ensure the template and UML/solution use the same method name so students can implement SealSaloon without compilation or API confusion.

issues.description: The Stock class method that adds a StockIngredient to the collection is named addToStockIngredients in the problem UML and in the solution, but in the template repository it is named addItem. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual operation (adding a StockIngredient to the stock) creates a mapping burden: students reading the problem statement/diagram will look for addToStockIngredients but find addItem in the starter code, which may cause confusion about which method to use or implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across artifacts. Rename the template's addItem(StockIngredient) method to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (or add a delegating addToStockIngredients method that calls addItem) so the template matches the UML in the problem statement and the solution implementation.
